text:
Lina (customer): hi, hitting 502/503s from the /v1/generate endpoint since ~09:35 PT. Started after our morning traffic spike. example response: {"error":"upstream error"} — can you check?
Emma S.: thanks Lina — sorry about this. i'm triaging, can you share request id or trace header?
Lina (customer): trace: x-trace-id=abc123; sample curl: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -H "X-Trace-Id: abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-13b"}'
Emma S.: got it. looping in SRE /eng. raj, marta — customer hitting 502/503 intermittently, looks correlated with rate-limiter errors per support logs.
Raj P.: on it. pulling gateway logs now. initial look: quota-gateway returning 502 to api-gateway because upstream connection to quota service hit socket-timeouts. stack: api-gateway -> quota-gateway -> quota-service/rate-limiter.
Raj P.: logs snippet: ```
ERROR quota-gateway: upstream error: dial tcp 10.42.7.33:8080: i/o timeout (after 5s)
WARN quota-gateway: returning 502 to client
```
Marta V.: interesting — we deployed a routing tweak at 09:30 that pins quota-gateway to the new internal network path (blue->green cfg). might be a misroute to a node with firewall rules.
Oliver (oncall): rollback flag ready. what do we need to validate before rollback? any risk to in-progress tokens?
Raj P.: safe to rollback to previous route (traffic to 10.42.5.x). temp mitigation: increase upstream timeout so connections don't immediately 502 while we fix route. but that only masks root cause.
Emma S.: Lina — we'll do rollback and keep you posted. timeframe ~5-10m. apologies for user disruption.
deploy-bot: Deploy 17685.2 started by Oliver (oncall) — rolling back route binding for quota-gateway.
Marta V.: quick repro steps i ran: 1) send burst of 50 concurrent requests with same API key 2) observe quota-gateway log `upstream socket timeout` 3) quota-gateway returns 502 and api-gateway bubbles 502 back. curl loop i used: ```for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer x" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done```
Raj P.: confirmed: iptables on the misrouted node blocked outgoing 8080 to quota-service; connection attempts timed out until conntrack freed entries. that's why we saw socket timeouts rather than immediate RSTs.
Oliver (oncall): rollback live. deploy-bot: Deploy 17685.2 succeeded — route binding reverted.
deploy-bot: Healthcheck: quota-gateway instances healthy (6/6) — latency normalizing.
Raj P.: post-rollback metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 3.8% -> 0.2% over 3m, upstream socket timeouts to zero.
Lina (customer): seeing good responses again, thanks. can you confirm whether any requests were charged incorrectly or double-billed?
Emma S.: good question — billing team please advise. for now we'll treat failed 5xxs as non-chargeable; we'll surface list of affected customers and replay logs to calculate token counts.
Marta V.: root cause: routing change deployed without validating iptables/firewall state on target node pool. change was intended to move quota-gateway to new AZ for capacity. fix: add e2e smoke that verifies upstream port connectivity before switching routes, and a preflight that checks node firewall rules.
Raj P.: action items: (1) postmortem draft, (2) add preflight check to deploy pipeline, (3) add a fallback that returns 4xx for quota rejections instead of 5xx on upstream timeouts (where possible), (4) notify billing.
Emma S.: Lina — i'll create a support ticket with timeline + impact and cc billing. estimate of affected window: 09:30–09:42 PT. we'll share token-level impact once billing runs script.
Oliver (oncall): adding runbook step: if quota-gateway upstream socket-timeout spikes, check route bindings + conntrack; if route misbound, rollback; if firewall rule present, open 8080 to quota-service.
Marta V.: will follow up with a small patch to quota-gateway: if upstream timeout occurs, classify as dependency-timeout (5xx) in logs but surface a clear code so that api-gateway can convert to 4xx when it's actually a quota denial vs infrastructure fault.
Raj P.: note for postmortem: some responses were 502 due to infrastructure misroute — customer-facing behavior was 5xx. we should avoid treating all quota failures as hard 5xx.
Emma S.: thanks team. Lina — truly sorry for the outage. we'll share the postmortem and the billing credit plan within 48h. happy to jump on a call if you want. :pray:
